top_stories.title: Cisco Zero-Day Highlights API Endpoint Authentication Issues
top_stories.summary: A maximum-severity authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-76460) has been discovered in Cisco's Identity Services Engine (ISE), receiving a perfect 10.0 CVSS score. The flaw targets API endpoint authentication, allowing attackers to bypass authentication controls in Cisco's NAC and identity management platform.

top_stories.title: The Pillar Cracks Three Ways: Azure Identity Infrastructure Takes Three Max-Severity Hits in One Patch Tuesday
top_stories.summary: Microsoft's September 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed three maximum-severity vulnerabilities targeting the Azure identity infrastructure, part of a record-breaking 964 CVE patch cycle. All three flaws targeted the Azure identity stack, representing a concentrated attack surface against Microsoft's cloud identity systems.

top_stories.title: Microsoft Entra Agent ID Expands with MCP Firewall, Adding Network-Level Control to Agent Governance
top_stories.summary: Microsoft is expanding its Entra Agent ID governance framework with the introduction of an MCP Firewall, adding network-level control to AI agent management. The new capability extends Microsoft Entra's identity governance to AI agents operating in enterprise production environments, providing security teams with additional controls over agent behavior and access.

top_stories.title: MFA Won't Save You From OAuth Consent Abuse
top_stories.summary: The article argues that MFA is insufficient to protect against OAuth consent abuse attacks, where attackers exploit delegated permissions rather than compromised credentials. The piece covers OAuth governance controls including least-privilege scopes, consent monitoring, and token revocation as necessary complementary measures.

top_stories.title: Microsoft reminds admins to migrate Entra ID users to passkeys
top_stories.summary: Microsoft has issued a reminder to administrators to migrate Entra ID users to phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, ahead of a policy change. SMS first-factor sign-in will be retired starting February 2027, with admins warned that failure to migrate will cause sign-in disruptions for affected users.

news.title: Passwork NIS2 efficiency guide: Save your team hours before the 2026 audit
news.summary: Passwork has published a NIS2 compliance efficiency guide aimed at helping organizations prepare for 2026 EU audit reviews. The guide addresses IAM implementation challenges highlighted by ENISA's 2025 report, which found 34% of EU organizations face severe IAM skills shortages under NIS2 requirements.

news.title: FBI's CJIS v6.1: What Security Teams Need to Know.
news.summary: The FBI updated its Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) Security Policy to version 6.1, introducing stronger requirements around encryption, vulnerability scanning, MFA, and identity management. Specops outlines the changes and provides guidance for agencies preparing for audits under the new policy.

news.title: Fake LastPass Authenticator Installer Abuses Microsoft-Signed Driver to Kill Antivirus and EDR
news.summary: Researchers at LastPass and Delphos Labs discovered a fake LastPass Authenticator installer on GitHub that deploys a Microsoft-signed Windows kernel driver to disable antivirus and EDR software before executing a password stealer. The malicious driver, signed through Microsoft's hardware compatibility program, scored zero detections on VirusTotal, making it a significant supply chain and credential theft threat targeting LastPass users.

news.title: Claude Opus 5 Helped Researchers Take Over OpenAI Staff Accounts via Chained Flaws
news.summary: Security researchers at Hacktron used Claude Opus 5 to chain two vulnerabilities—a bug in OpenAI's public help forum software and a weakness in OpenAI's login system—to take over ChatGPT and Codex accounts belonging to OpenAI employees. The attack chain ultimately granted access to an internal OpenAI code repository, demonstrating an account takeover via chained authentication and session flaws.

news.title: Okta Stock Is Up 132% Since March. Is the Stock Already Priced In?
news.summary: Okta stock has risen 132.5% since mid-March, with a 21% single-day jump on August 27 following a fiscal second-quarter earnings beat. Analyst ratings currently stand at 25 buys, 9 outperforms, 10 holds, and 1 underperform.

news.title: Identity Visibility in 2026: The Foundation of Identity Security
news.summary: An article explains the concept of identity visibility as a foundational element of modern identity security, referencing credential theft as a leading breach vector per Verizon's DBIR. The piece covers what identity visibility means in IAM contexts and why cloud and multicloud environments present complications for achieving it.

news.title: SolarWinds Patches ARM Hard-Coded Key Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
news.summary: SolarWinds has patched a high-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-28326, CVSS 8.8) in its Access Rights Manager (ARM) product that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution via a hard-coded key flaw. The flaw affects all versions of Access Rights Manager 2026.2 and prior.

news.title: CrowdSec Says TanStack npm Attack Led to Copy of 170 Private GitHub Repositories
news.summary: CrowdSec disclosed that an attacker copied approximately 170 private GitHub repositories on May 22 by using the credentials of a recently departed employee whose access had not been revoked. The breach originated from a supply chain attack on TanStack npm packages that stole credentials, highlighting failures in access deprovisioning and offboarding processes.

news.title: Microsoft Patches CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry Flaw Enabling Unauthorized Privilege Escalation
news.summary: Microsoft patched a maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) vulnerability in Azure AI Foundry, tracked as CVE-2026-85889, that allowed unauthorized privilege escalation over a network due to missing authentication for a critical function. The fix was applied server-side and requires no customer action.

news.title: SailPoint’s (SAIL) Falcon Next-Gen SIEM Arrangement Fits Its Broader Identity Security Push
news.summary: SailPoint expanded its strategic alliance with CrowdStrike, integrating with CrowdStrike's Falcon Next-Gen SIEM platform. The partnership connects SailPoint's identity governance capabilities with CrowdStrike's security operations tooling.

news.title: Jim Cramer Says AI Could Make Okta’s Security Software More Essential
news.summary: Jim Cramer discussed Okta on a September 16 episode of Mad Money, arguing that AI is making Okta's identity security software more essential rather than obsolete. The segment is a brief television commentary on Okta's market position rather than reporting any new product, financial, or operational development from the company.

news.title: Why Shares of Okta Stock Shot Up 10% This Week
news.summary: Okta's stock rose 10% this week, driven by positive market momentum among cybersecurity names and solid earnings results. The article covers Okta's financial performance as an enterprise authentication and identity platform.

news.title: jumpserver v5.0.0
news.summary: JumpServer has released version 5.0.0 of its open-source Privileged Access Management platform. The platform provides DevOps and IT teams with secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, database, and RemoteApp endpoints through a web browser.

news.title: Critical Check Point Management Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root
news.summary: A critical vulnerability in Check Point's Security Management and Log Servers allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute code as root. Check Point has released a patch via its LivePatch update channel and reports no known exploitation in the wild.

news.title: keycloak v26.7.4
news.summary: Keycloak has released version 26.7.4 of its open source identity and access management platform. The release continues Keycloak's support for modern applications and services with this minor version update.

news.title: vault v2.1.1
news.summary: Vault version 2.1.1 has been released as a tool covering secrets management, encryption as a service, and privileged access management. No specific details about new features, bug fixes, or breaking changes are provided in the description.

news.title: Implementing defense-in-depth authorization for MCP tools on Amazon Quick
news.summary: The article provides a technical walkthrough for implementing defense-in-depth authorization for Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. The implementation uses Microsoft Entra ID group and claims-based JWTs to enforce per-user, per-tool access controls.

news.title: Amplifier Extends Workforce Security to the AI Agents Employees Build and Use
news.summary: Amplifier Security announced Agent Intent & Posture Management, a new capability that connects discovered AI agents to employee owners, documents each agent's stated purpose, and guides risk remediation. The solution extends workforce security to AI agents built and used by employees, addressing identity and access governance concerns around agentic AI in enterprise environments.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. AI is being credited for accelerating vulnerability discovery, though security experts note organizations are struggling to prioritize testing and deploying the volume of fixes.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian driver's licenses, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has launched an official inquiry into the breach, which affects a widely-used identity verification provider.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian man Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges for hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage. The attacks involved credential-based unauthorized access to Snowflake customer accounts, resulting in data theft including over 100 million AT&T customer records.
